message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's morally acceptable for me to tell my cousin that his kid can't stay in our house. Let me break this down step by step. First, my cousin moved in with my husband and me. We made a separate flatlet for him by closing off the main bedroom and bathroom. So, he has his own entrance, and it's like two separate units in one house. That seems pretty set up for him to have his own space. Now, my cousin has a 2-year-old, and he's in the middle of a custody battle with his ex. He wants to spend more time with his son, and I completely support that. I really hope he gets more time with his son. Yesterday, he asked if my husband and I could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son. The thing is, there's no access from my cousin's room into our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. So, if his son is staying in our house, he can't get to him easily, and I'm not comfortable with that. I understand that the court is looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son. Honestly, his current room and bathroom are more than big enough. But I'm not comfortable letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin has no access to him. I'm not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that's just how my family is. Everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. But I'm wondering, would I be a bad person (WIBTA) for telling him I won't allow his son to stay in our house and potentially jeopardizing his court case? So, is it morally acceptable for me to say no? Or should I put my comfort aside and help him out, even if it makes me uncomfortable? I think about the consequences. If I say no, it might affect his custody case, which could mean he spends less time with his son. That's not good because I support him wanting to be with his child. On the other hand, I have my own boundaries and comfort levels. I don't feel safe or comfortable with his son staying in our house if he can't access him easily. Maybe there's a middle ground. Could we find another arrangement that makes everyone comfortable? Or is it more important to support my cousin in this situation, even if it means I have to compromise my own boundaries? I also consider the family dynamics. Everyone expects me to help, but I have to prioritize my own well-being too. It's a tough spot because I care about my cousin and his son, but I also need to respect my own limits. In the end, I'm trying to balance supporting my cousin with maintaining my own comfort and safety. It's not easy, but I need to decide what's more important in this situation.
